tasks.short: Compute energy use per square metre, look up benchmark data for the building type, compare and judge deviations, and put the comparison in the report.

steps.what: Energy auditor computes existing energy consumption levels per square metre in spreadsheets
Energy auditor looks up normative data for the building type
Energy auditor compares consumption to normative data and judges deviations
Energy auditor writes the comparison into the audit report

tasks.design: Code computes weather-normalised energy use per square metre from the meter data and floor area, and a benchmark table per building type is loaded as configuration, so the auditor does not build spreadsheets or look up figures. The comparison chart and table are generated into the report. Judging what a deviation means stays with the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Intensity was computed and benchmarks looked up by hand for each audit.
tasks.enabler_now: Normalisation and benchmark comparison are plain code over meter data.
tasks.still_hard: Benchmarks for mixed-use buildings are rough.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a high figure is a server room, not waste.
tasks.altitude: The auditor judges deviations instead of computing them.

reach.learn: Whether the building is above or below its peers.

evidence.claim: Ella Energy predicts normal use from meter data and flags deviations.

assumptions: Boundary: from usage data to the comparison written; recommendations are outside.
Input contract: benchmark table kept current; fallback is looking up.

Judging deviations stays with the auditor (s3 keeps its full time). s1 keeps 30 for checking meter gaps and the floor area; s2 keeps 40 for choosing the building type and looking up types the table lacks; s4 keeps 60 because the chart and table are generated and the auditor still writes the text on deviations.
Floor areas are known from the energy label or drawings.
research_questions: Do code results match the auditor's own calculations?

incremental.description: Energy auditor updates the benchmark table yearly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an unusual building that the benchmark table does not cover, so figures are looked up as today (26.5); high: an office or school covered by the table (41.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule installers and homes, oversee installation of insulation and other measures, record completed measures, and sign off the work.

steps.what: Household picks an installation slot online from the installers' shared planning
Energy auditor schedules installers and home visits: by phone today; after the change the auditor phones only households that do not book online
Energy auditor oversees installation of pipe insulation, weatherstripping and low-flow showerheads
Energy auditor records completed measures and materials: on paper forms today, in a job app after the change
Energy auditor signs off the completed work

tasks.design: Households pick an installation slot online from the installers' shared planning, so the auditor phones only those who do not book. The auditor records completed measures and materials in a job app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of on paper forms; this first record keeps its time. Overseeing installation and signing off stay with the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Slots were agreed by phone and measures recorded on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Online slot booking from an installer's shared planning is common.
tasks.still_hard: Older residents prefer to be called.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that the insulation hides damp that needs fixing first.

reach.learn: Whether fewer visits fail because nobody is home.

evidence.claim: OptiMiser's Nexus module keeps job records and quality checks.
GPS and time stamps in a crew app monitor attendance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from measures ordered to work signed off; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: installers keep their planning current; fallback is phone.
Households book online in about the time a call took (s0, share 1, household time).

Overseeing installation, recording completed measures and signing off keep their full time; recording in the app is a first record. s1 keeps 50 because about half of households book online and the auditor still phones the rest.

incremental.description: No new upkeep: phoning households that do not book is s1's remaining time, and the household's booking is step s0.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most residents in the programme prefer a call, so only a fifth book online (2.8); high: about half book online (7.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect income documents from applicants, compute household income against thresholds, judge eligibility, ask for missing documents, and record the decision.

steps.what: Applicant uploads income documents to the programme portal against the checklist
Energy auditor collects income documents from applicants: by e-mail and post today, from the programme portal after the change
Energy auditor types the income figures from the documents and computes household income against programme thresholds: in a spreadsheet today, in a threshold calculator after the change
Energy auditor verifies income eligibility of participants in the publicly financed program
Energy auditor writes requests for missing or unclear documents: by e-mail today; after the change the portal checklist shows applicants what is missing, so fewer requests are needed
Energy auditor checks each request: the documents named, the applicant and the address it goes to
Energy auditor sends the checked request to the applicant
Energy auditor records the eligibility decision and its reasons, with the calculator's per-rule result attached

tasks.design: Applicants upload income documents to the program portal against a checklist that shows what is still missing, so documents do not arrive scattered over e-mail and post. The auditor types the income figures from the documents into a calculator that holds the programme thresholds as configuration and shows the result per rule. Requests for missing documents are checked by the auditor before each is sent. The auditor judges eligibility and records the decision; no decision is made by software alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrived by e-mail and post and income was computed in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Portals with document checklists; threshold rules as configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Self-employed income is hard to read from documents.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a household whose income just changed.
tasks.altitude: The auditor judges cases instead of computing income.

evidence.claim: A subsidy decision made solely by automated processing falls under GDPR article 22.
AI used by a public body to judge eligibility for public assistance is high-risk under Annex III 5(a).

assumptions: Boundary: from the application to the decision recorded; payment of the subsidy is outside.
Input contract: thresholds set by the program; fallback is spreadsheets.
Applicants upload in about the time e-mailing took (s0, share 1, applicant time).

The auditor decides every case; judging, checking and sending requests keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because some documents still come by post; s2 keeps 70 because the auditor still types the figures and only the spreadsheet and threshold look-ups go; s4 keeps 50 because the checklist prevents about half of requests; s5 keeps 80 because only copying the computed figures into the record goes.

incremental.description: Energy auditor updates thresholds when the program changes.

approvals.approved_version: Each request for documents exactly as checked by the auditor in s4c, sent once to the applicant's address on the application; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many applicants are self-employed and send papers by post, so collecting and requests change little (16.5); high: most applicants use the portal (27.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The energy auditor keeps judging deviations, overseeing installations and deciding eligibility; spreadsheets, phone planning and scattered documents shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An auditor with more time with households.
